statement: A boot token reaches a `__setup` handler when its first strlen(option) characters equal the option string; the handler receives the rest of the token, value included. No check that the next character is `=` or end of token (that check exists only for early params).
quote: int n = strlen(p->str); if (parameqn(line, p->str, n)) {

statement: The comparison reads `-` as `_` on both sides, so `resume-offset=` selects `resume_offset=`.

An unknown `param=val` token is rejoined into `param=val` before the `__setup` search; dotted module-style names (`x.noresume=1`) only reach the search under their full name and so match no hibernation option.

`noresume` and `nohibernate` are registered bare and their handlers ignore the argument, so `noresume=0`, `noresume=1`, `noresumefoo` and `nohibernate=1` all set the flags. `noresum` (shorter than the option) does not.
`resume=` copies its value verbatim and each later token overwrites it (last wins); a `noresume` earlier on the line makes it return before copying.

An empty `resume_file` means no resume device: `find_resume_device` returns -ENOENT before any lookup. Its default is `CONFIG_PM_STD_PARTITION`, so an empty last `resume=` on this host leaves nothing to resume from.

resume_offset= changes the offset only when sscanf %llu converts; base-10 conversion stops at once without a leading decimal digit (no + , no - for unsigned), so resume_offset=abc keeps the earlier value; with a leading digit the conversion stops at the first non-digit, so resume_offset=4096k reads 4096 (simple_strntoull raw 79-95; its digit loop _parse_integer_limit is in lib/kstrtox.c, not pinned).

Across options, order matters only through noresume: before resume= the device is never copied (BP5); after it the resume initcall still bails out (1106-1112). Either way the image is not read; the gate reports HR-NORESUME-ARG and does not model where noresume sits. Within one option, order selects the winner (last wins, BP5, BP7), which the gate does model.
